summary: Iteration 14 validated WhatsBoost-only OTP/auth behavior with MOCKED provider calls, plus mobile UI/source checks for WhatsApp OTP copy and subscriber default preference behavior.
action_items: Optional cleanup: remove/retire unreachable MSG91/Traccar OTP code paths to reduce auth-surface confusion.
Optional refactor: split backend/server.py into smaller modules (>700 lines currently).
Keep real WhatsBoost delivery test deferred until recipient consent exists; current automated run intentionally uses MOCKED outbound provider calls only.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py is very large (~1500+ lines), exceeding maintainability threshold; split auth, payments, complaints, reminders, and notifications.
Legacy OTP provider functions (MSG91/Traccar) remain in file while current design is WhatsBoost-only OTP; this increases future regression risk if inadvertently re-wired.
seed_data_creation: No persistent seed credentials created. Temporary users/challenges were created and cleaned up within tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Credentials file was present and states no public demo credentials. Auth tests used short-lived local JWTs and mocked WhatsBoost HTTP calls only. Real WhatsApp delivery remains intentionally untested (no consented recipient).
rca_of_issue: No functional failures in scope after rerun. Initial test-script failures were due to brittle assertions (timezone-naive datetime comparison and overly specific profile-string check), fixed in test file only.
